title: Annotatio V §.X reply (2): Oral-fundamentality needs worn fiction Reformed deny presence; Beza
pass_a_gloss: To the latter: The Author sets in the open that his dispute for the Fundamental character of Oral Eating can otherwise gain no strength unless propped by the sufficiently worn fiction of presence of Christ’s body in the Holy Supper denied by the Reformed — a fiction utterly exploded and rejected even by Beza himself, cited here by our Disputant, when he writes that the Lord’s Sacred Supper is emptied if one does not confess Christ’s Flesh most present in the Supper by faith.
pass_b_english: Reply to the second: the Author himself shows his Oral-fundamentality case has no force unless propped by the worn fiction that the Reformed deny Christ’s bodily presence in the Supper.
Even Beza — whom the Disputant cites here — exploded that fiction, writing that the Lord’s Supper is emptied if one will not confess Christ’s Flesh most present in the Supper by faith.
source_text: Ad posterius: Autorem in aprico ponere, disputationem suam pro Oralis Manducationis Fundamentalitate, ullius roboris fieri aliter haud posse, quin suffulciatur protrito satis commentô de negata à Reformatis corporis Christi in S. Cœna, præsentia, etiam ab ipso Beza, Disputatori nostro hic loci allegato, prorsus explosô rejectóque, quando Sacram Domini Cœnam evacuari scribit, si minus quis per fidem, præsentissimam esse Christi Carnem, in Cœna fateatur.
